content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

Section 24 (Assignment and Change of Control) already meets our preferred ASSIGN position on every element:

| Element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Affiliate assignment without consent | § 24.1 |
| Successor (merger/reorg/acquisition/substantially-all-assets) without consent | § 24.1 |
| Vendor may not assign without our consent | § 24.2 (also captures delegation of material performance and Vendor's own change of control) |
| Consent not unreasonably withheld | § 24.2, § 24.3 |
| No Vendor assignment to a competitor | § 24.2 |
| No Vendor termination right on our change of control | § 24.4 |

Cross-checks confirmed no conflicting language: § 9 has no change-of-control trigger (§ 9.2 is insolvency-based with an express carve-out for lawful reorganization that does not impair performance); § 13.3 carries our licence rights to a permitted Affiliate/successor; § 30.5 recognises a permitted successor as an enforcing person; § 29.2 merely requires non-email delivery for assignment notices.

Two immaterial points noted in the rationale rather than flagged: the competitor bar reaches only a *direct* competitor, and it is qualified by "without Customer's consent" — since that consent gate is ours, it operates as optionality in our favour, not a gap. Per the playbook, a clause at or above the fallback is not redlined, so I have not upgraded this wording.
